**Paper:** figure style and variable names  ·  **Source:** [fluxpy/naming.py](https://github.com/FranzFlink/bacsam2-flux-analysis/blob/main/fluxpy/naming.py)

The variable names of the data files and the symbols of the manuscript (Table 1).

| variable | manuscript symbol | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `H_obs_ec` | H_S,obs,EC | airborne eddy-covariance reference (Sect. 3.1) |
| `H_obs_bulk` | H_S,obs,bulk | bulk, T-Bird in-situ inputs and KT-19 T_s |
| `H_rs_bulk` | H_S,RS,bulk | bulk, ERA5 column and MODIS T_s |
| `H_era_bulk` | H_S,ERA,bulk | bulk, ERA5 column and ERA5 T_s |
| `H_era_diag` | H_S,ERA,diag | ERA5 model-diagnosed surface flux |
| `H_car_diag` | H_S,CAR,diag | CARRA model-diagnosed surface flux |

**Conventions**

* Every `H_*` is positive UPWARD (surface to atmosphere). The ERA5 and CARRA
  products are positive downward and are sign-flipped ONCE, in
  [`scripts/calc_bulk_and_ec_fluxes.py`](#scripts/calc_bulk_and_ec_fluxes.py).
* Diagnostics use the same pathway tokens: `Ri_obs`, `Ri_rs`,
  `dtheta_obs`, `dtheta_rs`, `U_obs`, `U_era` (`dtheta` = theta_air -
  theta_s). Every `Ri_*` is the two-point bulk Richardson number of Eq. (B3).
* The segment file uses `sensible_heat_flux` for the EC flux; the pipeline
  output uses `H_obs_ec`.
